shortDescription: Home-sharing platform Airbnb NASDAQ:ABNB on Tuesday said it is expanding its grocery delivery service with Instacart NASDAQ:CART across the U.S., allowing guests to order groceries through its app ahead of their stays.Guests can place orders up to three weeks before check-in, with $0 delivery fees…

children: on Tuesday said it is expanding its grocery delivery service with Instacart
across the U.S., allowing guests to order groceries through its app ahead of their stays.
Guests can place orders up to three weeks before check-in, with $0 delivery fees on orders of $10 or more. The service does not require a separate Instacart
account or app, and the listing address is automatically populated. Airbnb
said the service will launch in Canada in the coming weeks.
In Phoenix, Arizona, and Orlando, Florida, hosts can also opt to receive grocery orders and stock the refrigerator and pantry before guests arrive.
said groceries have been one of its most requested services and that the expansion makes the offering available for the vast majority of stays in the U.S.
The company said it worked with Instacart

to analyze grocery orders by destination. Guests in Miami, Florida, ordered bottled yerba mate at more than 30 times the U.S. national average, while orders for oat milk in Los Angeles were more than twice the national rate.
In Canada, where the service is scheduled to launch in the coming weeks, Airbnb
said grocery orders around major holidays have included fresh-cut tulips, soil, and Canadian flags.
“We wanted groceries to feel like a natural part of a stay, not another errand,” Juan David Borrero, Airbnb’s
global head of partnerships and business development, said.

title: Airbnb enters grocery services with Instacart
